answer: Sybils can mint names, not uncorrelated work. Each identity holds at most one routing slot, kept only by emitting a live signal every epoch: a signature over a settled job receipt mixed with a public beacon drawn from a moving dune of salts that expires after one epoch and buries yesterday's transcript. The next admission token hash-chains that signal onto the last, winding a spiral eight turns deep. Clones that share a controller collide on receipt timing—jitter under 40ms is a slash—and any broken turn forfeits the eight-epoch bond and the slot.
